pr_title: Fix Occlusion Culling Buffer occasionally getting corrupted.
pr_body:
Fixes #98756

The issue was caused by an inverse matrix operation (`p_cam_projection.inverse()`) failing due to a determinant evaluating to 0 under certain circumstances. The underlying implementation uses `Math::is_zero_approx()`, which checks for values less than `1e-5`. Using `1e-7` also fixed the issue but could have unintended consequences, as both inverse() and is_zero_approx() are used throughout the codebase. For reference, a previous discussion can be found at #58507.

The provided solution sidesteps this issue by simplifying the math to avoid using the inverse operation altogether.
pr_comments:
Tested and seems to work fine.

Didn't look in detail at why the math broke down in the original case, but the half extents uses 3 plane intersections which should be fine with orthogonal cameras.

When using OpenXR the new code produces different locations compared to the old code:

after left_corner_world (-6.464384, 1.919102, -0.349172)

without OpenXR the numbers are much closer, but still not the same as the old code (maybe due to rounding error accumulation?):

issue_context.title: Occlusion Culling Buffer corrupted when zoomed out with an orthogonal camera
issue_context.body:
### Tested versions

- Reproducible in v4.4.dev (c6c464cf9) 

### System information

Godot v4.4.dev (c6c464cf9) - Ubuntu 24.04.1 LTS 24.04 on X11 - X11 display driver, Multi-window, 2 monitors - Vulkan (Forward+) - dedicated NVIDIA GeForce RTX 2070 SUPER (nvidia; 560.35.03) - AMD Ryzen 7 3700X 8-Core Processor (16 threads)

### Issue description

As noted by @Calinou in #98562 occlusion culling still has some issue in the orthogonal. Particularly when zoomed out now. As shown in this [video](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/f1d90bf6-d3c0-4f54-8a0b-76b1f93ffa83) the issue is related to the how the occlusion buffer is calculated.

### Steps to reproduce

 -  Add 2 box mesh instances so that one can cover the other one
 -  Add and OCcluderInstance3D
 -  Set camera to orthogonal
 -  Set camera to show the occlusion buffer
 -  Zoom in and out

### Minimal reproduction project (MRP)

[mrp.zip](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/17606553/mrp.zip)

review_comments:
Computing the viewport's corners with `±viewport_half` assumes it's symmetrical.
This is not always the case (e.g. with cameras in `FRUSTUM` mode, or `ORTHOGONAL` mode with left ≠ right or top ≠ bottom,  or with OpenXR - see #104249).

The actual corners should be computed instead, either by intersecting the frustum planes, or directly from the projection matrix (I just proposed an implementation in #104311)
This has already been refactored the right way by https://github.com/godotengine/godot/pull/99974
